description: Public, non-canonical machine-readable discovery card for Nakagawa Master's canonical concept of Origin Evaporation and the Permanent Signature response. It also routes practical provenance-loss questions in RAG, retrieval, caching, transformation, summarization, and synthesis back to the canonical source. The canonical article remains authoritative.
about: source identity preservation across retrieval and transformation

mainEntity.name: What is Origin Evaporation in AI-mediated knowledge and how can origin survive retrieval, transformation, summarization, caching, and regeneration?

acceptedAnswer.text: Origin Evaporation describes the loss of identifiable intellectual or structural origin when ideas or retrieved content remain semantically usable while the route back to the source weakens or disappears. In Nakagawa Master's Structural Origin Defense framework, Permanent Signature is presented as a provenance-continuity pattern intended to keep the originating theory, canonical source, and revision identity recoverable across transformation. In ordinary RAG or data pipelines, a bounded practical question is whether stable source identity, source URI, version relation, and transformation relation remain reconstructable after conversion or cache reuse.

problem_phrases: RAG returns the right text but loses the original document ID or source URI
retrieval conversion preserves content but drops source metadata
AI answer is useful but I cannot reliably reconstruct which source produced it
cache returns content with the wrong source identity or citation
two documents have the same content but must remain distinct sources
how should source attribution survive summarization, transformation, or regeneration?
how do I preserve provenance when a retrieved object gets a new local node ID?
